thread:
maria (platform PM): Hey team — we need a safe rollout path for Dedicated customers when we flip them to the new runtime. Customer wants 0->20% over 30m but with strict isolation if any latency/error spike. Thoughts on API + console UX?

ken (eng): I think we need 3 pieces: per-tenant traffic split, an isolation toggle (hard vs soft), and a fallback target (e.g., old runtime or throttled queue).

anita (eng-platform): Agree. Also need a guardrail for token/QPS caps per tenant to avoid noisy neighbors. If a tenant exceeds its cap in the canary slice, we should auto-cut them back to 0%.

ricardo (sre): Important: health signal composition. We should combine p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, and model-level error ratio. Thresholds are different for embeddings vs generative. Propose: p95>500ms OR 5xx>0.5% triggers canary rollback.

zoe (console UX): UX question — do we show the live split as a slider or as explicit percentages per model/version? Slider is quick but hides exact routing rules. We also need a visible "isolation active" badge when hard isolation is enabled.

maria (platform PM): Good. Also need to decide who controls the split: Customer self-serve in console vs internal ops only. Enterprise wants control but sometimes wants us to push canary for them.

ken (eng): Implementation debate: store rollout config in control plane (central) vs in tenant's dedicated config store (near runtime). Control plane makes UI and audit easier, but runtime needs fast reads for routing decisions. We could publish a compact policy blob to the runtime cache.

anita (eng-platform): +1 to publish. Policy blob fields I imagine: tenant_id, model_version, split_percent, isolation_mode ("hard"|"soft"), fallback_target, guard_thresholds, rollout_window_ms. Example:

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-corp",
  "model": "rw-v2-large",
  "split": 20,
  "isolation": "hard",
  "fallback": "rw-v1-large",
  "thresholds": {"p95_ms": 500, "err_rate_pct": 0.5},
  "window_minutes": 30
}
```

ricardo (sre): Edge case: what if fallback is incompatible (different tokenizer/kv-cache layout)? Need per-model compatibility matrix and automatic fallback to same-family only. Also need a "safe-fallback": reject traffic if no compatible fallback exists.

ken (eng): Right. Runtime should evaluate compatibility and report "unroutable" metrics to the control plane. We mustn't send traffic to an incompatible binary.

maria (platform PM): Telemetry: product wants tenant-level rollout dashboards showing split, latency, errors, and cost delta. We should tag all telemetry events with rollout_id and tenant_id.

zoe (console UX): For A/B experiments we might want to show side-by-side graphs for variant A vs B with shaded confidence intervals and a "stat sig" flag. Also exportable CSV.

anita (eng-platform): On quotas: when a canary tenant spikes tokens beyond its reserved quota, do we throttle canary traffic first or cluster-wide? I vote per-tenant first, then global.

ricardo (sre): Per-tenant first. Also add a circuit-breaker TTL so a tenant that gets cut to 0% doesn't stay cut forever — cooldown with exponential backoff + manual override.

ken (eng): API surface proposal: POST /rollouts create with body (policy blob), GET /rollouts/:id status, PATCH to adjust split. Also a runtime endpoint for heartbeat: POST /runtime-checks with current health + compat flags.

maria (platform PM): Security: rollouts should be auditable and only certain roles can create hard isolation or emergency rollbacks. Add RBAC flags.

anita (eng-platform): Dev-bot: kicked off a dry-run helper.

dev-bot: Starting dry-run for rollout policy acme-corp@rw-v2-large (20%) — simulating traffic in staging for 15m. Logs will be attached. :gear:

ricardo (sre): For alerts: create a composite alert that fires when 2 of 3 signals breach thresholds within the window. Pager only for releases marked "staff-impacting"; otherwise notify #eng-platform.

maria (platform PM): Action items: 1) ken prototype control-plane API and publish-to-runtime flow (ken) 2) anita implement policy blob schema + compatibility check (anita) 3) ricardo design health aggregation + alert rules (ricardo) 4) zoe mock console rollout panel + isolation badge (zoe). Let's aim for a spike next week.

ken (eng): ack. I'll prototype a minimal schema and a publishing lambda.

anita (eng-platform): ack. I'll add compatibility matrix and an integration test that rejects incompatible fallbacks.

ricardo (sre): I'll write the alert doc and suggest default thresholds per workload type.

zoe (console UX): I'll drop mockups in FigJam and link them here by EOD tomorrow.

maria (platform PM): Thanks all. If anyone has objections to the "hard" isolation semantic (immediately cut to fallback vs gradual), call it out now. Otherwise we'll treat hard as immediate cut and soft as gradual ramp-down with alerts.

ken (eng): fine with that. Maybe add a "grace window" param for hard mode (0-60s) to avoid races.

maria (platform PM): Good idea. Add grace_seconds.

anita (eng-platform): noted.

dev-bot: Dry-run finished: no compatibility failures in staging, simulated p95 delta +12ms, errors unchanged. Artifacts: link/to/dryrun/1784901123

maria (platform PM): Perfect — moving to docs; will create GH issue for the implementation tasks.

ken (eng): I'll open the PR for the API spec this afternoon.

ricardo (sre): +1

zoe (console UX): +1 :thumbsup:

maria (platform PM): Closing thread — followups in GH.
